site.name: tessera
site.summary: Tessera Fictional embedded SQL database official docs and function reference (PostgreSQL / DuckDB official-docs style). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Hero (title + slogan + Get started button + real syntax-highlighted SELECT SQL example); version switcher (v2.4 / v2.3 / v2.2 / v2.1); ⌘K search; three quick-start cards (Install / Connect / Your first query); 6 docs-section cards (Architecture / SQL Syntax / Functions / Data Types / Storage / Extensions); dark / light theme toggle. - `reference.html` — Reference main entry. **Three-column layout**: left deep TOC tree (Schemas / Tables / Views / Indexes / Functions [Aggregate / String / Numeric / Date-Time / JSON / Window sub-groups] / Operators [category sub-groups], nodes expandable / collapsible); center reference overview + popular links + v2.4 new-features callout; right-side on-this-page outline. - `function-date-trunc.html` — DATE_TRUNC function detail page (**canonical example spec**). explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full tessera system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: Tessera’s docs have a consistent three - column layout, but mobile usability issues exist. The 'Get started' button is a placeholder, and many tap targets are too small. Horizontal overflow occurs on mobile, and some links lack feedback. Only 3% of interactive features were tested, so there may be more untested issues.

exploration_plan.goal: Explore and critique the UX of the Tessera docs system, covering the main docs flow, reference pages, and key interactions across desktop and mobile.
exploration_plan.summary: Start with the home page (index.html) to validate navigation, theme toggle, and quick-start flows. Then explore the reference page (reference.html) and function detail pages (e.g., function-regexp-match.html, function-row-number.html) to check three-column layout, TOC, and code examples. Finally, verify mobile responsiveness and error-handling for failing pages (e.g., function-date-trunc.html).
assumptions: The site is a static docs site with no dynamic backend (except maybe search), so page loads should be fast except for failing pages.
The three-column layout on reference/function pages is consistent across valid pages.
risk_hotspots: small tap targets (per layout warnings, especially on mobile)

phases.title: Home Page & Core Interactions
phases.objective: Validate home page navigation, theme toggle, version switcher, and quick-start flows.
key_checks: Click theme toggle (🌓) to switch dark/light.
Interact with version selector (v2.4 / v2.3) to check responsiveness.
Click 'Get started' and 'View reference' buttons to verify navigation.
Test search button (⌘K) for interaction (even if search is dummy).
exit_criteria: All home page interactables tested, theme toggle works, version selector responds, navigation links to reference/index work.

phases.title: Reference & Three-Column Layout
phases.objective: Explore reference.html, check TOC, popular links, and three-column layout consistency.
key_checks: Expand/collapse left TOC (e.g., Functions > String sub-group).
Click popular links (e.g., DATE_TRUNC, REGEXP_MATCH) to check navigation.
Verify right-side 'On this page' outline and center content layout.
exit_criteria: Left TOC interactable, popular links navigate, three-column layout verified on desktop.

phases.title: Function Detail Pages (Valid)
phases.objective: Validate function detail pages (e.g., function-regexp-match.html, function-row-number.html) for content, code blocks, and examples.
key_checks: Check three-column layout (left TOC, center content, right outline).
Verify code blocks (signature, examples) and parameter tables.
Test 'Edit this page on GitHub' button (if present) for interaction.
exit_criteria: Function pages load with valid content, code blocks/syntax highlighting (if present) are visible, examples are formatted.

phases.title: Other Reference Pages (Operators, Data Types, SQL Select)
phases.objective: Explore operators.html, data-types.html, sql-select.html to check content structure and navigation.
key_checks: Check left TOC structure (e.g., Operators > Arithmetic sub-group).
Verify content organization (e.g., SQL SELECT syntax on sql-select.html).
Check for consistent three-column layout (if applicable).
exit_criteria: All target reference pages loaded, content structure verified, TOC interactable.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Error Handling
phases.objective: Test mobile viewport for key pages, validate small tap targets, and check error pages (e.g., function-date-trunc.html).
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport, re-test theme toggle, version selector, and navigation.
Check small tap targets (e.g., search button, version selector) for usability on mobile.
Attempt to load function-date-trunc.html again to check error handling (e.g., 404 or fallback content).
exit_criteria: Mobile viewport shows responsive layout, critical interactables (theme, version, navigation) work, error page (if any) has meaningful fallback.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages (excluding failing ones initially, then re-validate failing pages if possible).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible controls (theme, version, TOC, buttons, links) on key pages.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks (navigation, theme, version, TOC) on mobile viewport for index.html, reference.html, and one function page.

notes: Failing pages (function-date-trunc.html, function-json-extract.html) need re-validation to check if load error is persistent or temporary.

findings.user_goal: Navigate and interact with the docs on mobile
findings.problem: Horizontal overflow on mobile viewports (e.g., page width 443px > viewport 390px) causes content to be cut off or require horizontal scrolling, which is not user - friendly.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in mobile viewports show page width exceeds viewport width (e.g., 'Page width 443px exceeds viewport 390px' in function - date - trunc.html).
findings.why_it_matters: Users on mobile devices will have a hard time accessing and reading all the content, which can lead to frustration and a poor user experience.
findings.suggestion: Optimize the page layout for mobile by using responsive design techniques like fluid grids, flexible images, and media queries to ensure the page fits within the mobile viewport width.

findings.problem: Many tap targets (e.g., 'Tessera' link, 'DATE_ADD' button) have dimensions below the 44px mobile guidance, making them hard to tap.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings show tap targets like 'Tessera' (100x26px), 'DATE_ADD' (318x42px) are below 44px height or width.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets increase the chance of mis - taps, leading to a frustrating experience for mobile users trying to interact with the docs.
findings.suggestion: Increase the size of tap targets to at least 44x44px by adjusting CSS properties like padding, margin, or font size for interactive elements.
findings.source_hint: function - date - trunc.html (mobile viewport), index.html (mobile viewport)

findings.user_goal: Start using Tessera by following the 'Get started' flow
findings.problem: The 'Get started' button on the home page is a placeholder (href = '#') and doesn't navigate to a tutorial or setup guide, blocking users from starting the onboarding process.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Get started' button changes the URL to index.html# but doesn't navigate to a new page with setup content.
findings.why_it_matters: Users looking to start using Tessera can't access the necessary onboarding information, preventing them from achieving their goal of getting started with the product.
findings.suggestion: Update the 'Get started' button’s href to point to a valid tutorial or setup guide page (e.g., a 'getting - started.html' page with step - by - step instructions).

findings.user_goal: Interact with quick - start and documentation cards to access related content
findings.problem: Quick - start cards (e.g., 'Your first query', 'Architecture') and some function links (e.g., 'DATE_ADD') don't provide visible feedback (URL change, visual state change) when clicked, making it unclear if the interaction was successful.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Your first query' card, 'Architecture' card, or 'DATE_ADD' link results in no visible URL change or interaction feedback.
findings.why_it_matters: Lack of feedback leaves users unsure if their action was registered, leading to confusion and repeated clicks, which is a poor user experience.
findings.suggestion: Add visible feedback like URL changes, visual animations, or state changes (e.g., color change, icon update) to interactive cards and links. For links, ensure href points to valid pages; for cards, add proper event handlers to trigger navigation or content display.
findings.source_hint: index.html: ux - 14, ux - 15; function - date - trunc.html: ux - 10

findings.user_goal: Use the docs with assistive technologies
findings.problem: A form field (version selector) on the reference page has no label, aria - label, or placeholder, making it hard for screen - reader users to understand its purpose.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings show a form field (select element) with no label, aria - label, or placeholder.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen - reader users rely on labels to understand form fields. Without a label, they may not know what the version selector is for, leading to accessibility issues.
findings.suggestion: Add a label, aria - label, or placeholder text to the version selector form field to describe its purpose (e.g., 'Select Tessera version').

findings.user_goal: Explore all interactive features of the Tessera docs
findings.problem: Only 3% of visible interactive feature signatures were exercised, meaning most features (e.g., many function links, data - type links) remain untested and may have usability issues.
findings.evidence: Coverage data shows 'feature_coverage_percent' is 3, with many unexplored features like 'ABS', 'Arithmetic', 'ARRAY_AGG' links in data - types.html.
findings.why_it_matters: Untested features may have bugs, poor design, or accessibility issues that could negatively impact the user experience, but these issues are currently unknown.
findings.suggestion: Conduct more comprehensive testing of interactive features by systematically clicking on links, buttons, and form fields across all docs pages to identify and address usability issues.

gaps: Only directly exercised 3% of visible interactive feature signatures.
39% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
